 ONCOR AND LCRA TSC’S RESPONSE TO KEVIN KENNEDY’S MOTION TO REQUEST
 RECONSIDERATION OF 59182 SOAH ORDER NO. 24 AND 59475 SOAH ORDER NO. 12

       On May 8, 2026, the State Office of Administrative Hearings (“SOAH”) Administrative

Law Judges (“ALJs”) issued an order (the “Order”) denying Mr. Kevin Kenndy’s request for a

continuance and granting in part Mr. Kennedy’s request to consolidate Public Utility Commission



                                             -1-
 of Texas (“Commission”) Docket Numbers 59182 and 59475.1 On May 12, 2026, Mr. Kennedy

filed a motion requesting that the ALJs reconsider their Order. Pursuant to 16 Tex. Admin. Code

(“TAC”) § 22.78, Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Services

Corporation (together, “Applicants”) timely file this response.

        Most of the arguments in Mr. Kennedy’s motion for reconsideration are the same that were

made in his Motion for Continuance. The ALJs are familiar with the parties’ positions, so the

Applicants need not belabor those points.2 Mr. Kennedy’s motion for reconsideration relies heavily

on his claim that the ALJs did not consider his 59-page Response to Applicants’ Response to Mr.

Kennedy’s Motion for Continuance.3 Mr. Kennedy is not entitled to a reply under Commission

procedural rules, so failure to consider his 59-page reply is not improper. Nevertheless, Mr.

Kennedy’s reply lacks merit for the same reasons discussed in Applicants’ Response to Mr.

Kennedy’s Motion for Continuance. So even if Mr. Kennedy was entitled to file a reply, which he

was not, the error would be harmless. Mr. Kennedy’s request for reconsideration should be denied.
